name: stat-panel
title: Official Record Stat Panel
description: RHS 820px translucent 'official record' panel that slides over track-1 footage and lists disaster facts, ending on a counted death toll. The most-reused sub-comp in the show (28 uses).

name: title-card
title: Episode Title Card
description: Stacked centered title reveal: cold-open hook line, punch line, full episode title (Arial Black 128), and a Georgia-italic amber date/brand subline.

name: outro-brand
title: Warning Hour Brand Outro
description: Closing 'THE WARNING HOUR' wordmark card with episode-number line and CTA tag, fading to black.

name: numbers-rollup
title: Stacked Numbers Roll-up
description: Header plus up to four rows of counted big Courier New figures with caption labels, closing on a source citation.

name: bulletin-typewriter
title: NWS Bulletin Typewriter
description: Green-on-black CRT typewriter reconstruction of a verbatim government bulletin, typed phrase-by-phrase in sync with narration, blinking cursor, verbatim-source label.

name: ranked-bars
title: Ranked Row Comparison
description: Masthead plus up to 3 fill-animated ranked rails with counted numeric readouts, a scale axis with ticks, and a record badge + closing kicker on the winning row.

name: ef-ladder
title: EF-Scale Rung Ladder
description: Two-column explainer: damage-indicator tile grid building one at a time, plus a rating ladder of wind-speed rungs, closing on a verdict stamp and reasoning line. Note: ep4 has a richer damage-indicator/scale treatment (g-scale.html, g-fujita.html, g-metmap.html) not extracted here.

name: stat-timeline
title: Chronology Rail Strip
description: Horizontal chronology strip: title, a two-endpoint-year growing progress rail stalling on a percent readout, then sequential narration-order text beats. Use this for a simple two-endpoint percent-fill rail; for a real multi-year event-by-event chronology with stacked per-year blocks and a card carousel, use event-timeline.html instead (added ep-enderlin-2025).

name: joplin-stat-panel
title: Joplin Stat Panel (worked example)
description: The stat-panel exemplar taken through the full pick-and-tweak flow for a real brief (Joplin 2011 casualty hit): search index, copy, hand-retune copy/counter, timings untouched. Reference for how library items become episode graphics.
params: derived from stat-panel.html — see that exemplar for the editable slots

name: moves-demo
title: Move library demo (roof panel throw)
description: 10 s worked example of moves.js: camera rig, arc throw, counter driven by the flight, shake, dust, measure-draw, clean exit. Copy moves.js inline; README lists every move.
params: see moves/README.md for each move's opts

name: webgl-tornado
title: WebGL Tornado (Three.js funnel, seek-driven)
description: Stylised funnel, wall cloud, debris and storm sky in Three.js, driven only by the paused GSAP timeline. No text: put labels on a HUD comp above it. Mount steps and CONFIG fields in webgl/README.md.
params: CONFIG block: scheme, seed, funnelWidth, height, rotationSpeed, path, debrisDensity, duration, cameraMove

name: master-map-us-canada
title: US+Canada Regional Map, Camera Pull-Out
description: Real, geographically-accurate regional basemap (Natural Earth 50m admin-1 states/provinces + the US-Canada land boundary, public domain) with a local damage-path overlay, a camera that pulls from ground-level local view out to the full regional map, lon/lat-projected place pins and an RHS credit-card rail. The channel's reference build for 'use a real US+Canada map' (owner 27 Sep 2026). Highest reuse value of this drop: every future episode needs a location map.
params: rlabs country/city labels (lon/lat-projected x,y via the header's formula, never eyeballed)
lon group second city + elie special pin (droppable)

name: split-shared-scale
title: Two-Storm Split Card, One Shared Rating Scale
description: Two events side by side, never merged into one card, both judged against a single rating scale drawn once on the centre divider so the same fact is never duplicated per side. Each side can carry its own evidence (an instrument readout, a day counter, a document reveal); drop whichever side-extras don't fit the beat.
params: p5/p3 shared-scale rung labels (and their SVG y-positions if rungs change)

name: quote-card
title: Verbatim Attributed Quote Card
description: Full-frame beige cite card over dark ground: a verbatim, attributed quote revealed phrase by phrase on the voice, with an optional second quote that swaps in after the first lifts out. The channel's beige cite-card treatment for quoting a real source (CLAUDE.md: never fabricate a quote, always attribute).
params: q1/q2 quote text (phrase spans, one per reveal beat)
q2 + its script block droppable for a single-quote card

name: event-timeline
title: Multi-Year Event Chronology Strip
description: A true stepped-label multi-year chronology: a year axis with per-event blocks stacked by year, a rotating card slot naming the current event as an axis pointer travels, then a trailing gap-since-the-last-one bar with a running day counter. The richer alternative flagged as missing from stat-timeline.html's own description; use this for a real event-by-event chronology, stat-timeline.html for a simple two-endpoint percent rail.
params: y07..y25 tick labels + axis year span (recompute the column-x formula in the script if the span changes)
b* stacked event blocks (left/top per event)
c*/t*/pl/dt event cards (one per event, in order)
bar/edge/end/cnt/gap/ef4 trailing gap-bar + counter target + closing labels

name: then-now-scale
title: Rating-Scale Then/Now Comparison
description: Two-column old-scale-vs-new-scale comparison on a shared wind-speed axis: a rating band grows on the old column then slides across and down onto the new column's lower threshold, closing on a swept-away house sketch. Reusable for any 'a standard changed, here's what moved and why' beat, not only the Fujita-to-EF-scale story it was built for.
params: wind axis ticks + mph-to-y formula in the script

name: radar-beam
title: Radar Beam vs Curved Earth Diagram
description: Full-frame SVG physics diagram: a radar station, its beam and a curved-earth ground line, showing why the beam rises above ground level with distance and misses the near-surface wind at a distant storm. Schematic, not to scale. The standard 'the rating comes from damage, not radar' explainer beat for any severe-weather episode.
params: in-diagram labels (Not Seen / Beam Height Rises With Distance / Radar)
